children: , the NAND-flash and data-storage producer, received a bullish Wall Street push Tuesday after Rosenblatt initiated coverage with a Buy rating and a $2,400 price target. Shares surged approximately 6.6% to $1,884.05, putting the stock within striking distance of the analyst's target after another sharp leg higher.

The AI angle is getting harder to ignore. Barron's reported that Rosenblatt analyst Kevin Cassidy sees NAND becoming a more important piece of the computing stack as AI workloads expand beyond processors and into massive pools of high-speed storage. Sandisk is already riding that cycle: fiscal fourth-quarter revenue reached $8.97 billion, up 51% sequentially, while management continues to lean into enterprise solid-state drives and its manufacturing partnership with Kioxia. The GuruFocus picture adds an interesting wrinkle: Sandisk's GF Score sits at just 51 out of 100, with standout growth and financial strength offset by much weaker GF Value and momentum readings.

At $1,884.05, Rosenblatt's $2,400 target implies roughly 27.4% additional upside. That is still substantial, but the market has already swallowed a meaningful piece of the bullish thesis. From here, the story gets tougher. Sandisk needs strong NAND pricing, disciplined industry supply and a richer enterprise mix to turn today's excitement into durable earnings power. AI-driven storage demand can keep the runway open, but executionnot scarcity headlineswill determine how much of that $2,400 target investors ultimately get.

title: Sandisk Jumps 6.6% as $2,400 Target Prices AI Storage Scarcity
